content.title: Who is Dan Serafini? Ex-MLB pitcher is arrested in 2021 Lake Tahoe-area murder case
content.text: Former Major League Baseball pitcher Dan Serafini, 49, and 33-year-old Samantha Scott were both arrested in Nevada Friday, Oct. 20, in connection with a fatal shooting that happened in the Lake Tahoe Area in 2021. | PREVIOUS COVERAGE | 'We are horrified': Family seeks justice after deadly Lake Tahoe-area shootingOn June 5, 2021, Serafini's father-in-law, 70-year-old Robert Gary Spohr, was killed by a single gunshot wound, and his mother-in-law, 68-year-old Wendy Wood Spohr was shot twice and hospitalized, officials said. Wendy Wood Sophr later killed herself on March 9, 2023, according to reporting from the San Francisco Chronicle. Her daughter Adrienne Spohr told KCRA 3 in a statement that despite an “incredible recovery, she missed my dad terribly and was never able to comfortably live again in her home in Lake Tahoe.”| RELATED COVERAGE | ‘My parents can finally rest in peace’: Daughter grateful for arrests in 2021 Tahoe-area murder caseSerafini, who has appeared on a reality show, is married to another one of the victims' daughters, Erin, and Scott had a close connection to the family, according to officials. Here is what else we know about the two suspects. What do we know about Dan Serafini? Serafini attended Serra High School in San Mateo and was drafted to the MLB in 1992. He pitched in the majors from 1996 to 2007 and played for the Minnesota Twins, Chicago Cubs, San Diego Padres, Pittsburgh Pirates, Cincinnati Reds and Colorado Rockies.He was suspended for 50 games after the 2007 season for testing positive for performance-enhancing drugs.Serafini spoke to SFGate in 2013 and said the steroid in his system was prescribed by a doctor in Japan while he was recovering from a torn Achilles tendon.Serafini did not return to the MLB but did continue playing baseball for teams in Mexico.In 2013, Serafini opened a bar in Sparks, Nevada, that was later featured on an episode of the reality show "Bar Rescue."According to a promotional video for the show, Serafini had lost $14 million through a series of bad investments and a divorce settlement before convincing his parents to take out a $240,000 loan against their house to buy The Bullpen bar. “When I first opened the bar, it was unbelievable. We were packed every night doing about $45-50,000 a month in sales. It was awesome,” Serafini said.But as the staff continued to party he became $300,000 in debt, according to the show. Bar Rescue reported that sales increased after the consultation and publicity, but the bar ultimately closed a few years later.In June 2021, Placer County deputies were investigating a gruesome mystery -- who shot and killed Robert Spohr and severely injured his wife. At the time, there were few clues.Several days after the attack video surveillance footage from the home and on West Lake Boulevard captured a man wearing a hoodie and face-covering and walking to the home several hours before the shooting.Two years later, investigators now believe that the man in the hoodie was Serafini. He was arrested in Winnemucca and Scott was arrested in Las Vegas with the assistance of various law enforcement agencies. Placer County officials said that Serafini and Scott waived extradition.Serafini and Scott have since been sent to jail in Placer County.Adrienne Spohr said her parents had been “incredibly generous” to her sister Erin and Serafini during their marriage. She shared a photo of them during a visit to Hawaii. What do we know about Scott? Officials described Scott as well-known to the family and said she is believed to have been a nanny at some point.Adrienne Spohr said Scott was a close friend of her sister's. “When I learned on October 20th that my sister’s husband Daniel Serafini and sister’s close friend Samantha Scott were arrested for the shooting of my parents, I was shaken to my core,” Spohr said in a statement. “This was a heinous, calculated crime. My parents had been incredibly generous to Daniel Serafini and Erin Spohr throughout their marriage. Despite being pressed for my opinion, I cannot comment on my sister’s level of involvement at this time.”Erin Spohr, who is listed in the lawsuit as a resident of Reno, has not been accused of a crime by the sheriff’s office or arrested. But Adrienne has also accused her sister Erin of involvement in her parents' death. She named her as a defendant along with Serafino in a wrongful death lawsuit that was filed in June. What do we know about a possible motive? The Placer County Sheriff's Office has not said what a possible motive is in the shooting.
